decisions.finding: The pale fork/tip projects farther up-left and the trailing pale shard descends farther than the Source shape. The gray/green material also becomes a gritty bright fringe. The material texture is real, but it does not excuse the visible pale-geometry displacement.

The Source has a broad dark-green field around the central brown cavity. Native1 turns much of that field into gray/brown dark rubble; thin bright green threads at3/4 do not retain the same broad green material readability. Brown/root relief is also substantially stronger.

The right-side brown branching center is retained, but its surrounding dark-green bands turn nearblack/olive-brown at native1. Higher scales show fine green threads while the Source broad green connections remain visually reduced; still a material-role mismatch.

The Source upper-left and lower green surround is readable as a broad dark-green area. In the new native1 it becomes mostly brown/black around pronounced brown root-like relief, with sparse brighter green filaments higher up. New detail does not preserve the green ground role.

The small upper-right green corner/contact collapses to dull olive-gray fragments at native1 amid brighter gray chips. The jagged black center remains recognizable and actual3/4 material is detailed, but the Source green corner readability is not retained across all scales.

The upper-left green contact remains plainly readable at native1 and higher scales, and the jagged gray/black floor layout remains recognizable. Actual3/4 show continuous chipped mineral structure and fine grit beyond SourceNN/noise-only finish. Brighter/harder gray exposure, stronger incised relief and native1 softness remain qualifications; genuine neighboring joins/context are still unreviewed.

The Source upper-right dark-green patch is broad enough to identify, but the new native1 leaves a gray/brown sliver and nearblack texture in that corner. Higher-scale scattered green specks do not restore the Source material field; the diagonal dark-floor striation is a stronger local interpretation.

The Source broad upper green field and gray contacts become an olive-brown/char center at native1 with disconnected bright moss threads at3/4. The gray fragments are more exposed, but the broad green material reading and proportions are materially shifted.

qualifications: Genuine continuous mineral/brown branching material is visible at native3/4 throughout; technical/artistic material existence does not repair displaced pale geometry or lost green roles.

3050a qualifies with stronger chipped/exposed gray relief, fine-grit contrast, native1 softness and local green brightness interpretation. It requires its own genuine context and Source-role review before any admission.
